userStories.title: Runner picks up the ACP text-run separator
userStories.description:
**Goal** — Upgrade the paired runner agent dependencies so assistant text separated by a tool call remains readable.

**Motivation** — These are the last open findings of the A-Z run. Each is small, but together they make the app look unfinished: glued agent text.

**Approach** — `apps/runner/package.json` dependencies.
- Baseline: `"@nathapp/nax-agent": "0.92.0"`, `"@nathapp/nax-agent-acp": "0.92.0"`.
- Target: both `"0.92.15"`, exact pins as today. `bun.lock` at the repo root is regenerated by `bun install`. `@nathapp/nax-agent-acp@0.92.15` declares the peer `@nathapp/nax-agent ^0.92.15`, so the two move together. `@nathapp/nax-ai` is not a direct runner dependency; it moves transitively with `nax-agent` in `bun.lock`.

Bump `@nathapp/nax-agent` and `@nathapp/nax-agent-acp` in `apps/runner/package.json` to exact `0.92.15`, and run `bun install` from the repo root so that `bun.lock` matches. Fix only what the new types force in runner code.

Add a fake ACP agent fixture: a Bun script speaking newline-delimited JSON-RPC 2.0 over stdio.
- It answers `initialize` and `session/new`.
- On `session/prompt`, it sends the `session/update` notifications its scenario names, then answers `{ stopReason: "end_turn" }`. The scenario is chosen by an environment variable passed through `acpBackend`'s `env`.
- It ignores `session/cancel` (a notification needs no reply), answers any other request with a JSON-RPC "method not found" error, and exits when its stdin closes.

Add a real-process test (no database, not gated on `KODA_DB_TESTS`) that:
- opens an `AgentSession` through `createAgentSession({ backend, profile: 'ask', workdir, tools: [], transcriptStore: createMemoryTranscriptStore() })`, the same options the runner's ACP probe passes (`apps/runner/src/capabilities/acp-agent-probe.ts:140-142`). Here `backend` is `acpBackend({ agent: { name: 'fake', command: process.execPath, args: [<fixture path>] }, allowUnsandboxed: true, env: { ... } })`, and `workdir` is a temporary directory made with `mkdtemp` and removed after the test;
- iterates `session.send(<prompt>)` to its last event, which is `turn_end`, and reads that event's `output` (the final round's text, `TurnResult.output`);
- closes the session.

The fixture path is resolved with `path.join(__dirname, ...)`.

**Scope** — In: the paired exact pins, generated root lockfile, new fake ACP process and actual AgentSession text-output regression proof. Out: API/web presentation work (US-002–US-008); any runner code change beyond what 0.92.15 types force; manual runner context correction, deployed runner restart and live-page checks.

**Interface** — `createAgentSession({ backend, profile: 'ask', workdir, tools: [], transcriptStore: createMemoryTranscriptStore() })`; `acpBackend({ agent: { name: 'fake', command: process.execPath, args: [<fixture path>] }, allowUnsandboxed: true, env: { ... } })`; `TurnResult.output` from the last `turn_end`.

**Test implementation** — Create apps/runner/test/fixtures/fake-acp-agent.ts and test/integration/acp-text-runs.integration.spec.ts. Use the actual package integration, not a local string-joining imitation. The first scenario must fail on 0.92.0 and the adjacent-chunk scenario is a regression guard that passes there too. Run bun run type-check, bun run test and bun run test:integration with the bumped pins; the new real-process spec needs no KODA_DB_TESTS. Close sessions and clean temporary workdirs even on failure.
acceptanceCriteria: [integration] Given the fake agent sends, in order, an agent_message_chunk with text 'Checking the file.', a tool_call with toolCallId 't1', a tool_call_update for 't1' with status 'completed', and an agent_message_chunk with text 'Done.', the last event yielded while iterating session.send(<prompt>) through createAgentSession and acpBackend is turn_end with output equal to 'Checking the file.\n\nDone.' (two newline characters). This fails on 0.92.0, which yields 'Checking the file.Done.'.

[integration] Given the fake agent sends two agent_message_chunk updates 'Hello ' and 'world' and no tool call, the last event yielded while iterating session.send(<prompt>) is turn_end with output equal to 'Hello world'. This is a regression guard: it passes on 0.92.0 too, and pins that no separator is added without a tool call.

routing.reasoning: A bounded paired-package upgrade uses the same actual AgentSession/backend construction as session-factory.ts and acp-agent-probe.ts; the session-integration security override retains strict test isolation, while complexity stays medium because no new production execution path is introduced.

userStories.title: Thread titles on dashboard and home jobs
userStories.description:
**Goal** — Carry threadTitle through existing dashboard and home read models and their generated API contracts.

**Motivation** — These are the last open findings of the A-Z run. Each is small, but together they make the app look unfinished: raw ids.

**Approach** — Dashboard job rows (`apps/api/src/fleet/dashboard/`).
- Baseline: `JOB_SELECT` and `RECENT_SELECT` in `prisma-dashboard.repository.ts` select no thread. `DashboardJobRow`, `DashboardRecentRow` (`dashboard.types.ts`), `DashboardActiveJobView`, `DashboardRecentJobView` (`dashboard-view.ts`), `DashboardActiveJobDto` and `DashboardRecentJobDto` (`dto/fleet-dashboard.dto.ts`) carry no `threadTitle`.
- Target: both selects add `thread: { select: { title: true } }`. The rows, views and DTOs carry `threadTitle: string | null`: the thread's title, or `null` when the job has no thread. `activeView` and `recentView` copy it. The DTO property is `@ApiProperty({ type: String, nullable: true })`.

Home jobs (`apps/api/src/home/`).
- Baseline: `findFailedJobs` and `findBlockedJobs` in `prisma-home.repository.ts` select no thread. `HomeJobRow`, `HomeJobView` (`home.types.ts`) and `HomeJobDto` (`dto/home-dashboard.dto.ts`) carry no `threadTitle`.
- Target: both selects add `thread: { select: { title: true } }`, and `toJobRow` maps `thread?.title ?? null` to `threadTitle`. The mapper destructures `thread` out, so the raw relation object does not leak into the row through the existing `...r` spread. The dashboard mappers do the same. `QUEUED_SELECT` spreads `JOB_SELECT`, so the queued window gains the join too; that is harmless. `buildHomeView` copies it into each `needsYou.jobs` entry, and `HomeJobDto` documents it as above.

After the API contract changes, `bun run generate` from the repo root regenerates `openapi.json` and the CLI client (`apps/cli/src/generated/types.gen.ts`).

`FleetJob.thread` in `apps/api/prisma/schema.prisma` is a Prisma relation to `ChatThread` (`threadId` -> `id`, `onDelete: SetNull`). Selecting `thread: { select: { title: true } }` reads the title in the same query.

**Scope** — In: dashboard/home selects, closed row projections, required nullable row/view/DTO field, generated OpenAPI/CLI types, additive fixture updates and behavioral/contract tests. Out: web cells and web helper widening (US-003), all other polish stories, requester-name fields and widening the DTO command enums. No schema migration or new title-fetch route.

**Interface** — `threadTitle: string | null`; `thread: { select: { title: true } }`; `@ApiProperty({ type: String, nullable: true })`. The data seam is GET /api/fleet/dashboard, GET /api/projects/{slug}/fleet/dashboard and GET /api/home. A dashboard or home job whose thread was deleted (`threadId` set null) has `threadTitle` null; US-003 owns the web fallback.

**Test implementation** — Add dashboard view ACs in src/fleet/dashboard/dashboard-view.spec.ts; its closed-world active/recent toEqual assertions gain only threadTitle:null and its recent() row fixture gains the required null default. Add threadTitle:null to src/common/test-helpers/fleet-dashboard.ts dashJob(), src/home/home.types.spec.ts job() and src/home/home.service.spec.ts job(); keep their existing assertions unchanged except the two specified dashboard closed-world additions. Extend test/integration/fleet/fleet-dashboard-repository.integration.spec.ts and test/integration/home/home-api.integration.spec.ts, extending the latter's local jobs response type with threadTitle:string|null. Keep existing integration cases unchanged and isolate new seeded rows so earlier exact-list/count tests are not affected. Preserve canRunDbTests and verify PG behavior outside the sandbox through the scoped host test command; a skip is not verification. Add the two nullable-property checks beside existing checks in src/fleet/fleet-openapi.contract.spec.ts and create src/home/home-openapi.contract.spec.ts. Root bun run generate must generate rather than hand-edit artifacts; review that the diff carries only threadTitle for DashboardActiveJobDto, DashboardRecentJobDto and HomeJobDto, including their required lists, without command enum changes.

userStories.title: Web job feature cells use the thread title
userStories.description:
**Goal** — Display thread titles consistently on dashboard, home and job-log surfaces through the existing shared feature-label helper.

**Motivation** — These are the last open findings of the A-Z run. Each is small, but together they make the app look unfinished: raw ids.

**Approach** — Web job types and the label helper.
- Baseline: `DashboardActiveJob` and `DashboardRecentJob` (`apps/web/lib/fleet-dashboard-types.ts`) and `HomeJob` (`apps/web/lib/home-types.ts`) have no `threadTitle`. `jobFeatureLabel` takes a full `FleetJobDto`.
- Target: the three types gain `threadTitle: string | null`.
- `jobFeatureLabel` takes `JobLabelInput = { command: string; feature: string; threadTitle: string | null }`, exported from `fleet-job-labels.ts`. A structural `command: string` is required because the three types declare `command: string` (`fleet-dashboard-types.ts:65,88`, `home-types.ts:36`), while `FleetJobDto.command` is the `FleetJobKind` union. `FleetJobDto` stays assignable to it.
- `isConfigJob` widens from `Pick<FleetJobDto, 'command'>` to `{ command: string }`. `CONFIG_KINDS` is already `readonly string[]`, so only the signature changes.

Job feature cells.
- Baseline: `ActiveRunsTable.vue:51`, `RecentRunsList.vue:47` (`components/fleet/dashboard/`) and `HomeNeedsYou.vue:97` print `job.feature`. The logs page subtitle (`pages/[project]/fleet/jobs/[id]/logs.vue:183`) is `${job.feature} | ${job.command}`.
- Target: each prints `jobFeatureLabel(job, t)` in place of `job.feature`. The logs subtitle becomes `${jobFeatureLabel(job, t)} | ${job.command}`.
- This also changes REVIEW and FIX rows to `PR #<n>` and config jobs to the config label on these surfaces, which matches the jobs list. The ACs pin the THREAD and RUN cases.

`jobFeatureLabel(job, t)` in `apps/web/lib/fleet-job-labels.ts` returns:
- the config label for config jobs;
- for `THREAD` jobs, `threadTitle` when it is non-blank, otherwise `t('fleet.jobs.threadFeature')` ("Thread");
- `PR #<n>` for `review-pr-<n>` REVIEW and FIX jobs;
- otherwise `job.feature`.

`useFleetJobs(slug).get(jobId)` (single-job GET). It already returns `threadTitle`, and the logs page uses it.

**Scope** — In: three web job types, exported minimal label input, isConfigJob signature widening and four feature text consumers. Out: API field population and generated contract work (US-002), preference/forms/board/a11y work (US-004–US-008), requester names, attention subjectName and system-note text. Do not add a fetch on the log page or modify requester/preserveJobLabels semantics.

**Interface** — `JobLabelInput = { command: string; feature: string; threadTitle: string | null }`; `jobFeatureLabel(job: JobLabelInput, t: Translate): string`; `isConfigJob` accepts `{ command: string }`.

**Test implementation** — Add the minimal-input case to tests/lib/fleet-job-labels.spec.ts, preserving existing helper cases. Extend tests/components/fleet-dashboard-tables.spec.ts, tests/components/home-needs-you.spec.ts and tests/pages/fleet-job-logs-page.spec.ts. Dashboard/home job fixtures gain threadTitle:null; all existing feat-<id>, ordinary RUN feature and non-THREAD subtitle assertions remain unchanged. Render untrusted titles as text. This story consumes US-002's data on GET /api/fleet/dashboard, GET /api/projects/{slug}/fleet/dashboard and GET /api/home; logs consumes its already-existing single-job title. A dashboard or home job whose thread was deleted (`threadId` set null) has null title and displays t('fleet.jobs.threadFeature').

userStories.title: Browser approval notifications move to settings
userStories.description:
**Goal** — Replace the ambiguous header bell toggle with a named browser-approval preference shared between settings and notification delivery.

**Motivation** — These are the last open findings of the A-Z run. Each is small, but together they make the app look unfinished: a header icon nobody can name.

**Approach** — Browser approval notification preference.
- Baseline: the preference lives inside `useApprovalRequestNotifications`, which returns `{ refresh, decided, enabled, supported, toggleBrowserNotifications }`. `components/fleet/ApprovalBadge.vue` renders the toggle (`data-testid="fleet-approval-notifications"`, BellRing / BellOff icons) in the header.
- Target:
  - A new composable, `useBrowserApprovalNotificationPreference()` in `composables/useBrowserApprovalNotificationPreference.ts`, owns the preference. It returns `{ supported, enabled, permissionDenied, toggle }`.
  - The state is shared per tab through `useState` (key `browser-approval-notification-preference`), so the settings page and the badge's notices read the same value without a reload.
  - It keeps today's storage key, its on-mount read, the permission request on enable, the user-id reset, and the "storage is optional" handling: when `localStorage.setItem` throws, `enabled` still changes for this tab.
  - `permissionDenied` is part of the shared state, not a computed over `Notification.permission` (which is not reactive). It is set to `Notification.permission === 'denied'` on mount and again after every `toggle()`.
  - `useApprovalRequestNotifications` reads `enabled` and `supported` from it, and no longer returns `toggleBrowserNotifications`.
  - Both callers, `useApprovalRequestNotifications.ts` and `pages/settings/notifications.vue`, import it explicitly from `~/composables/useBrowserApprovalNotificationPreference` (no reliance on Nuxt auto-import), so tests can alias the module.
  - The settings section sits outside the page's load-state branches (`LoadingState` / `loadFailed` / `v-else`), because it reads only local browser state.
  - The checkbox's `change` handler awaits `toggle()`, then sets the input's `checked` back to `enabled.value`, so a refused permission leaves the box unchecked.
  - `ApprovalBadge.vue` no longer renders the toggle, and drops the `BellOff` / `BellRing` imports.
  - `pages/settings/notifications.vue` gains a section (`data-testid="settings-browser-approval-notifications"`) with the heading `t('notifications.browser.title')`. It has a checkbox (`id="settings-browser-approvals"`) with a `<label for="settings-browser-approvals">` reading `t('notifications.browser.approvals')`, bound to `enabled` and calling `toggle()` on change.
  - When `supported` is false, the section shows `t('notifications.browser.unsupported')` in place of the checkbox. When `permissionDenied` is true, it shows `t('notifications.browser.denied')` under it.

`useApprovalRequestNotifications(counts)` in `apps/web/composables/useApprovalRequestNotifications.ts`:
- It keeps the browser-notification preference in `localStorage` under `koda-approval-notifications-<userId>`.
- It reads that key on mount, together with `Notification.permission === 'granted'`.
- It resets the preference when the user id changes.
- `deliverBrowser` sends nothing unless `enabled` and `supported` are both true.

These existing preference responsibilities move to the new shared owner; toast/inbox reconciliation and account-change notice cleanup remain in the notices composable. `pages/settings/notifications.vue`: the notification preferences page (per-category in-app and email switches).

**Scope** — In: new preference owner, shared reactive state, explicit caller imports, local settings UI, removal of only the header toggle, and both locales. Out: toaster/auth changes (US-005), other UI polish stories, server preferences/approval authorization, moving or rearranging other header controls, and removing the now-unused fleet.approvals.notifications.enable/disable keys.

**Interface** — `useBrowserApprovalNotificationPreference()` returns `{ supported, enabled, permissionDenied, toggle }`; shared `useState` key `browser-approval-notification-preference`; existing storage key `koda-approval-notifications-<userId>`.

**Copy (both locale files)** — notifications.browser.title: en "Browser notifications", zh "浏览器通知". notifications.browser.approvals: en "Show a browser notification when an approval is waiting for me", zh "有待我处理的审批时显示浏览器通知". notifications.browser.unsupported: en "This browser does not support notifications.", zh "此浏览器不支持通知。". notifications.browser.denied: en "Notifications are blocked for this site. Allow them in your browser's site settings.", zh "此网站的通知已被阻止。请在浏览器的网站设置中允许。".

**Failure handling** — No Notification API renders unsupported text and no checkbox. Refused enable leaves enabled false and shows denied text. Throwing localStorage preserves the tab-only choice. Preserve identity fencing around an asynchronous permission request and SSR-safe initialization.

**Test implementation** — Create tests/composables/useBrowserApprovalNotificationPreference.spec.ts and move existing preference/toggle tests there from useApprovalRequestNotifications.spec.ts; retain notices tests for shared enabled/supported gating and in-app toasts. Pin two concurrent callers sharing useState without remounting. Alias the new module explicitly in tests/pages/notification-settings-page.spec.ts AND notification-settings-touch-target.spec.ts to refs for supported/enabled/permissionDenied plus a toggle spy; otherwise their mount reaches missing Nuxt/browser globals. Keep existing page cases. Replace fleet-approval-badge.spec.ts's old toggle click test with absence of fleet-approval-notifications and drop toggleBrowserNotifications from its stub. Remove only that control's obsolete touch-target case from fleet-approval-badge-touch-target.spec.ts; badge-link checks stay. The shared preference is the seam by which toggling in settings affects badge notices without reload. Preserve deliverBrowser's hidden-tab-only gate and existing refresh/decidability/expiry/deduplication gates: notification-delivery ACs use a mounted caller, a signed-in user, a positive counts snapshot and an unexpired, unannounced request the user may decide. The positive browser case also supplies a hidden document, supported true and granted permission.
acceptanceCriteria: [unit] useBrowserApprovalNotificationPreference mounted for user 'u1', with Notification.permission 'granted' and localStorage key koda-approval-notifications-u1 set to 'true', reports enabled true.
[unit] toggle() from disabled, with Notification.requestPermission resolving 'granted', sets enabled true and stores 'true' under koda-approval-notifications-u1.
[unit] toggle() from disabled, with Notification.requestPermission resolving 'denied' (and Notification.permission then 'denied'), leaves enabled false.

[unit] Given a disabled useBrowserApprovalNotificationPreference mounted for user 'u1', when toggle() receives 'denied' from Notification.requestPermission and Notification.permission is then 'denied', permissionDenied is true.
[unit] toggle() from disabled, with permission 'granted' and localStorage.setItem throwing, sets enabled true for the tab.

[unit] After toggle() on one useBrowserApprovalNotificationPreference caller enables the preference, a second caller in the same tab (sharing the useState key browser-approval-notification-preference) reports enabled true without remounting.
[unit] When the auth user id changes from 'u1' to 'u2', enabled becomes false.

[unit] Given a mounted useApprovalRequestNotifications with a signed-in user, counts.value.total equal to 1, and a new, unexpired, previously unannounced pending request the user may decide, when refresh() lists that request with shared enabled false, no browser Notification is created and its in-app toast still appears.

[unit] Given a hidden browser tab, shared supported true and enabled true, Notification.permission 'granted', and a mounted useApprovalRequestNotifications with a signed-in user, counts.value.total equal to 1 and a new, unexpired, previously unannounced pending request the user may decide, when refresh() lists that request, exactly one browser Notification is created.
[unit] ApprovalBadge renders no element with data-testid='fleet-approval-notifications'.

[unit] pages/settings/notifications.vue with supported true renders, inside settings-browser-approval-notifications, a checkbox with id 'settings-browser-approvals' and a label whose for is 'settings-browser-approvals' and whose text is the notifications.browser.approvals text.
[unit] When a change event fires on the settings-browser-approvals checkbox in pages/settings/notifications.vue with supported true, the shared browser preference's toggle() is called once.
[unit] pages/settings/notifications.vue with supported false renders the notifications.browser.unsupported text and no checkbox in that section.
[unit] pages/settings/notifications.vue with permissionDenied true renders the notifications.browser.denied text in that section.

routing.reasoning: Extracts shared lifecycle-aware state across concurrent callers, optional persistence and async browser permission. Strict isolation applies to identity-dependent opt-in and user-switch fencing, while approval access-control rules remain unchanged.

suggestedCriteria: When an enable request resolves after the auth user changes, the new account's enabled preference stays false.
When the settings checkbox change awaits refused permission, the input's checked value is restored to false.
When the remote notification-preference load fails, the browser-notification settings section remains visible.
When shared supported is false, a new pending approval still raises its toast but creates no browser Notification.
When persistence throws after enabling and another caller subsequently mounts in the same tab, both callers continue to report enabled true.

Without it, the page setup reaches `useState` and `Notification`, which the harness does not provide. AC-11 to AC-14 are added, and the existing cases stay unchanged.
the mount aliases the new preference composable module to the same stub, for the same reason. The existing assertions stay unchanged.
the four new `notifications.browser.*` keys from the Design table.
the same four keys in Chinese.

the case at line 376, which clicks `fleet-approval-notifications` and expects `toggleBrowserNotifications` to be called once, is replaced by a case asserting the badge renders no `fleet-approval-notifications` element. The `notifications` stub drops `toggleBrowserNotifications`.
the touch-target case for `fleet-approval-notifications` (lines 18-24) is removed, because the control leaves the badge. The badge link's own touch-target checks stay.

preference and `toggleBrowserNotifications` cases move to the new composable's spec (see Creates). The cases left here assert that `deliverBrowser` respects the shared `enabled` and `supported` values.

userStories.title: Toast position and auth page copy
userStories.description:
**Goal** — Keep toasts away from header account controls and make the sign-in/reset journey copy and recovery navigation clearer.

**Goal** — Make large profile suggestions searchable and grouped, remove misleading cost guidance, and reveal hidden ticket matches.

**Motivation** — These are the last open findings of the A-Z run. Each is small, but together they make the app look unfinished: a misleading cost hint and PR chip.

  - The grouping comes from a new pure helper, `groupSuggestionsByPrefix(names: readonly string[]): Array<{ prefix: string; names: string[] }>`. A name's prefix is the text before its first `-`, when that text is non-empty and a non-empty remainder follows that first `-`. So `native-ds` has prefix `native`, while `-x`, `native-` and `fast` have none. Every name without a prefix goes to the group with prefix `''`, whose heading is `t('fleet.dispatch.profileGroupOther')` ("Other" / "其他").
  - Groups are sorted by prefix in plain code-unit order (the default string comparison), with `''` last. Names keep their input order within a group.

userStories.description:
**Goal** — Reveal off-screen ticket-board columns and distinguish a closed pull request from a closed/rejected ticket.

**Motivation** — These are the last open findings of the A-Z run. Each is small, but together they make the app look unfinished: a misleading cost hint and PR chip.

**Approach** — Board scroll hint (`components/TicketBoard.vue`).
- Baseline: `<div class="overflow-x-auto">` with no hint.
- Target:
  - The scroll container keeps `overflow-x-auto` and gets a template ref.
  - A new pure helper, `boardScrollHints(m: { scrollLeft: number; clientWidth: number; scrollWidth: number }): { left: boolean; right: boolean }` in `lib/ticket-board-scroll.ts`, decides the hints. `right` is `scrollLeft + clientWidth < scrollWidth - 1`, and `left` is `scrollLeft > 0`. A non-finite input yields `false` for that side.
  - The component keeps the result in a ref, filled by a `measure()` function that reads the container's three fields. `measure()` runs on mount, on the container's `scroll` event (a template `@scroll` listener) and on window `resize`. The mount-time call is not pinned by a test (the harness has no layout at mount); the scroll and resize paths are.
  - When `typeof window !== 'undefined'`, the `resize` listener is added with `window.addEventListener('resize', measure)` on mount and removed with `window.removeEventListener('resize', measure)` on unmount. Without a `window` (SSR, or a node test mount with no fake window such as `board-layout.spec.ts`), both steps are skipped and nothing throws.
  - Test harness note: `tests/helpers/mount-sfc.ts` renders fake nodes with no layout fields, and its mount `globals` do not reach a bare `window`.
    - Component tests set `scrollLeft`, `clientWidth` and `scrollWidth` on the container's fake node, then fire its `scroll` handler.
    - A test that needs `window` assigns a fake with `addEventListener` / `removeEventListener` spies to `globalThis.window` before mounting, and deletes it in `afterEach`, as `tests/composables/useProjectInvites.spec.ts` does.
    - The helper itself carries the arithmetic.
  - When `canScrollRight` is true, a right-edge overlay renders (`data-testid="board-scroll-right"`). It is a gradient from `bg-background` plus a `Button` with a `ChevronRight` icon and `aria-label` `t('tickets.board.scrollRight')` ("Show more columns" / "显示更多列"). Clicking it calls the container's `scrollBy({ left: 300, behavior: 'smooth' })`.
  - The same applies on the left edge with `canScrollLeft`, `data-testid="board-scroll-left"`, `ChevronLeft`, `t('tickets.board.scrollLeft')` ("Show earlier columns" / "显示前面的列") and `left: -300`.

- Target:
